claims.text: ExxonMobil's article "Technology and people driving the next generation of drilling in the Permian" is dated October 26th, 2026.
Exxon believes the technology could eliminate roughly one-third of high-consequence drilling incidents.
claims.quote: We believe this technology has the potential to eliminate roughly one-third of high-consequence drilling incidents.

claims.text: Handling heavy drill pipe historically required workers on the rig floor, and mechanical arms and robotic systems can now perform much of that work.
claims.quote: Activities such as handling heavy drill pipe have historically required workers on the rig floor ... Now, mechanical arms and robotic systems can perform much of that work, reducing workers' exposure to higher-risk tasks.

claims.text: Exxon expects similar staffing levels on automated rigs and calls the technology a force multiplier, not a replacement, letting people focus on oversight, decision-making and equipment optimization.
claims.quote: ExxonMobil expects to maintain similar staffing levels while enabling employees to focus on higher-value activities. | we view the technology as a force multiplier, not a replacement. | allow our people to focus on oversight, decision-making, equipment optimization and other higher-value work

claims.text: Exxon plans to automate more than half of its unconventional drilling fleet by year-end 2028.
claims.quote: plans to automate more than half of our unconventional drilling fleet by year-end 2028

claims.text: Automated rigs are one of more than 50 technologies being deployed across Exxon's Permian operations.
claims.quote: Automated rigs are just one of more than 50 technologies being deployed across ExxonMobil's Permian operations

claims.text: Exxon aims to raise Permian production to approximately 2.5 million oil-equivalent barrels per day by 2030.
claims.quote: our goal of increasing Permian production to approximately 2.5 million oil-equivalent barrels per day by 2030

claims.text: Exxon's article cites recent demonstrations of H&P's FlexRobotics technology as a picture of the future of drilling.
claims.quote: Recent demonstrations of H&P's FlexRobotics® technology highlight what the future of drilling can look like:

claims.text: Exxon operates more than 30 drilling rigs in the Permian Basin.
claims.quote: Exxon, the largest oil producer by volume in the U.S., operates more than 30 drilling rigs in the Permian Basin, two of which are automated rigs with robotic equipment.

claims.text: Exxon's first automated rig drilled two miles horizontally underground in a little over six days, the third fastest time in Exxon's history.
claims.quote: It drilled two miles horizontally underground in a little over six days, the third fastest time in Exxon's history.

claims.text: Helmerich & Payne supplied Exxon's first automated rig, installed the year before the August 2026 Reuters report.
claims.quote: The company installed its first automated rig, supplied by drilling contractor Helmerich & Payne, last year.

claims.text: In west Texas an Exxon contractor sits in a small office on the rig and uses screen controls to run robotic machinery moving steel pipes weighing roughly 2,000 pounds.
claims.quote: In rural west Texas where oil rigs and pump jacks dot the sparse flat landscape, an ExxonMobil contractor sits in a small office on a drilling rig, using controls on a screen to operate robotic machinery and move tall steel pipes weighing roughly 2,000 pounds.

claims.text: Two of Exxon's Permian rigs were automated as of the August 2026 report.
claims.quote: operates more than 30 drilling rigs in the Permian Basin, two of which are automated rigs with robotic equipment

claims.text: On one of Exxon's automated rigs in Midland, a gate surrounds the drilling floor with a Red Zone sign and a drawing of the Grim Reaper.
claims.quote: On one of Exxon's automated rigs in Midland, a gate surrounds the drilling floor with a sign reading "Red Zone: Restricted Area." A drawing of the Grim Reaper illustrates the risk that workers face around heavy equipment and pressurized systems.

claims.text: Robotic arms now position drill pipe columns over two stories tall and connect them to the drill string, work workers used to help do.
claims.quote: Where workers would usually help move columns of drill pipe over two stories tall, robotic arms now position the pipes and connect them to a drill string. This allows drilling to continue deeper into the wellbore.

claims.text: Rig employees communicate with Exxon's central operations team in Houston to set the robotic system's movements.
claims.quote: Employees on the rig communicate with Exxon's central operations team in Houston to determine the precise movements the robotic system should make.

claims.text: Exxon's Bart Cahir said about a third of significant injuries in well drilling happen on the rig floor.
claims.quote: "In the history of well drilling activity, about a third of significant injuries that occur happen on the rig floor," he said. "By getting people out of that higher risk area, we're essentially eliminating that risk."

claims.text: Exxon plans automated rigs for a quarter of the fleet the year after the report (2027) and half by 2028.
claims.quote: Exxon plans to expand automated rigs to a quarter of the fleet next year and then half of the fleet by 2028, Cahir said.

claims.text: Cahir, Exxon's senior vice president of unconventionals, called taking people off the rig floor the productivity play.
claims.quote: "When we take people off the rig floor, those same individuals are now able to think ahead and plan for the next operation and that combination gives us efficiency," he said. "This is the productivity play."

claims.text: Exxon plans to grow Permian production by almost 40% to reach 2.5 million barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2030.
claims.quote: Exxon plans to grow its Permian production by almost 40% to 2.5 million barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2030.

claims.text: On October 7th, 2026, H&P said it will deploy seven more FlexRobotics systems for Exxon over the next 12 months, bringing the total to nine.
claims.quote: October 07, 2026 (WO) — Helmerich & Payne (H&P) will deploy seven additional FlexRobotics systems for ExxonMobil over the next 12 months ... The new deployments will bring the total number of FlexRobotics systems operating for ExxonMobil to nine, following the deployment of the first two systems on H&P rigs.

claims.text: H&P says FlexRobotics automates repetitive rig-floor activities, reducing personnel exposure to higher-risk tasks.
claims.quote: FlexRobotics® technology automates repetitive rig-floor activities

claims.text: FlexRobotics was developed with NOV and runs on three Yaskawa six-axis robotic arms.
claims.quote: Developed in collaboration with NOV, this breakthrough system features a three-arm robotic platform | powered by three Yaskawa six-axis manipulators

claims.text: One arm tails pipe stands to the well center, one cleans, dopes and aligns the connection, and one racks pipe in the derrick board.
claims.quote: L1 tails stands to or from the setback area to either the well center or the mousehole | L2 cleans, dopes, aligns the pipe connection | U1 racks the pipe into the derrick board, or delivers pipe to the elevators.

claims.text: H&P says FlexRobotics delivers consistent 1:40 slip to slip connections while keeping crews out of the red zone.
claims.quote: delivering consistent 1:40 slip to slip connections while helping keep crews out of the red zone

claims.text: Sliding gate barriers stop the robotic system if a gate is opened, and the driller works from an improved chair and console with a joystick.
claims.quote: Sliding gate barriers will e-stop RTX system if gate is opened. | Improved driller chair with optimized console | Updated joystick and handle for floor wrench and drawworks allowing the driller to keep more focus on the rig floor

claims.text: In the robotics packages, the driller supervises and initiates processes that the robots then execute along preplanned paths.
claims.quote: The driller supervises the operations and initiates processes for the robotics to execute. The machines' environments are mapped out with preplanned paths for each sequence of handling drilling tubulars and casing.

claims.text: A drill pipe connection on a typical land rig is usually handled by one derrickhand and two floorhands.
claims.quote: the workers who handle drill pipe and equipment during a connection – usually one derrickhand and two floorhands – are regularly multitasking on top of making the connection

claims.text: H&P's first FlexRobotics rig, FlexRig 618, sat at H&P's facility in Galena Park, Texas, before deploying to the Permian.
claims.quote: taken from H&P's facility in Galena Park, Texas, where Rig 618 was located prior to deployment.

claims.text: Bart Cahir is Exxon's senior vice president of unconventionals and spoke in an interview on the rig.
claims.quote: said Bart Cahir, Exxon's senior vice president of unconventionals, in an interview on the rig.

claims.text: The Reuters report counting two automated Exxon rigs is dated August 24th, 2026, with a photo of an automated rig in Midland, Texas.
claims.quote: Reuters | Aug 24 2026 at 10:04 AM | An automated oil drilling rig operated by ExxonMobil in Midland, Texas, August 17, 2026.

claims.text: Exxon's article says automation is not about replacing people.
claims.quote: Automation is not about replacing people.

cautions: No source calls FlexRobotics or Exxon's automated rigs AI. Say robots and automation.

The one-third figure is Exxon's belief about potential, not a measured result. Cahir's separate stat is that about a third of significant injuries historically happen on the rig floor. Keep the two distinct.
2,000 pounds is roughly, for tall steel pipes moved by the robots.
Two miles in a little over six days was Exxon's first automated rig, the third fastest time in Exxon's history.
Staffing is an expectation, not a guarantee.
Midland and west Texas come only from the Reuters report reprinted by AJOT.
